facts.text: Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79 and buried the Roman town of Pompeii.
Ash and pumice fell on Pompeii for many hours before surges of scorching gas and ash swept through the town.
Systematic excavation of Pompeii began in 1748.
The ash preserved painted walls, thousands of graffiti and carbonized loaves of bread in a bakery oven.
In the 1860s, archaeologist Giuseppe Fiorelli poured plaster into hollows left in the ash by decayed bodies, creating casts of victims.
The plaster casts have been altered and restored many times since they were made.
DNA from several casts overturned old stories: an adult with a gold bracelet holding a child, long called a mother, was an unrelated man.
Many residents appear to have fled during the early hours of the eruption.
Painted election notices survive on Pompeii’s walls, including one backing a candidate because he brings good bread.
About one third of ancient Pompeii is still unexcavated.
